newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Global steel output falls 0.4 percent in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Global steel output falls 0.4 percent in 1996.

text.p: Global crude steel production fell to 750.4 million metric tonnes in 1996, 0.7 percent down from 1995, the International Iron and Steel Institute said on Tuesday.
"This decrease mainly reflects reduced production in Europe and Japan, nearly balanced by strong performance in North and South America and in Asia," it said in a statement.
China was the world's top steel producer in 1996, with an output of 100.4 million tonnes -- up 5.2 percent from the previous year.

Output fell 4.4 percent in Western Europe to 162.8 million tonnes and 2.8 percent in Japan to 98.8 million tonnes. It rose 0.7 percent in North America to 123.5 million tonnes, although it fell 0.6 percent in the United States to 94.6 million tonnes.

The slump in Europe reflected "the lack of dynamism in the construction in other sectors," while that in the United States reflected blast furnace outages and a decline in exports coupled with a significant increase in imports, especially from Europe, the institute said.

Production rose 2.8 percent in South America to 35.6 million tonnes, influenced by intensified trade between Latin American countries, and 2.2 percent in Asia to 290.1 million tonnes, including a rise of 5.7 percent to 38.9 million tonnes in South Korea.
Eastern Europe's output dropped 10.4 percent to 30.6 million tonnes, while South America's rose 2.8 percent to 35.6 million tonnes.
The institute also reported that global crude steel output rose 5.2 percent in December compared with a year earlier, to 61.2 million metric tonnes.
Output rose 11.6 percent in Western Europe to 13.2 million tonnes, 0.7 percent in the United States to 7.9 million tonnes and 1.1 percent in Japan to 8.4 million tonnes
The annual figure reflects total world steel production, while the monthly figure is based on reports from 67 steel-producing countries, the institute said. -- Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
